1	# SWO Website — Claude Code Project Context
2	
3	## Mission
4	Build a responsive, product-first public marketing landing page for Smart Workout Optimizer (SWO) in this standalone repository.
5	
6	## Before coding
7	1. Read `README.md` and every relevant file in `docs/`.
8	2. Inspect the supplied images in `references/`; do not substitute unrelated/generated screenshots for authentic SWO UI.
9	3. Check the current project files and toolchain before choosing or changing the stack.
10	4. Keep work limited to the frontend/design system, structured content, subagent creation, and custom skill creation.
11	5. Token tracking is implemented and verified — see **Token tracking** below. Do not claim a token figure without re-running the collector.
12	
13	## Current state (Phase B complete)
14	Phases run in order, each gated on user approval:
15	
16	| Phase | Status |
17	|---|---|
18	| A — inspect and plan | Complete |
19	| B — toolchain bootstrap + token/session tracking | **Complete and verified** |
20	| C — design tokens, component specs, content schema, subagent, skill | Not started (awaiting approval) |
21	| D — landing-page implementation | Not started (requires a separate instruction) |
22	
23	No application code, design tokens or page sections exist yet. `src/` has not
24	been created. Do not start Phase C or D work without explicit instruction.
25	
26	## Toolchain (verified on this machine)
27	Windows 11 · Node v26.2.0 · npm 12.2.1 · Git 2.55 · Claude Code 2.1.153.
28	Node runs TypeScript natively, so `scripts/*.ts` execute without a loader.
29	
30	Installed so far: `typescript`, `vitest`, `@types/node`. Phase C adds React,
31	Vite, Tailwind, Zod, lucide-react and sharp. Ask before adding anything else.
32	
33	## Commands
34	```bash
35	npm run track:usage   # collect Claude Code token/session usage -> tracking/
36	npm test              # Vitest suite (17 tests, synthetic fixtures)
37	npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
38	```
39	
40	## Token tracking
41	`scripts/track-usage.ts` parses Claude Code's local JSONL session transcripts in
42	`~/.claude/projects/e--Projects-Airtribe-PM-SWO-Project` and writes
43	`tracking/usage-ledger.json`, `tracking/usage-ledger.csv` and
44	`tracking/usage-summary.md`. Parsing logic lives in `scripts/lib/usage-parse.ts`.
45	
46	Essentials before touching or quoting it:
47	
48	- **Deduplicate by `requestId`.** One API response is written as several
49	  assistant lines sharing one identical `usage` object. Summing lines inflated
50	  real totals ~2.2×. This is the collector's core correctness property.
51	- `total_tokens = input + output + cache_creation + cache_read`. These four are
52	  disjoint as reported, so cache reads are counted once.
53	- `thinking_tokens` is a **subset** of `output_tokens`; never add it.
54	- Nothing is ever estimated from characters or words. Missing fields are `null`,
55	  never `0`.
56	- Read-only on `~/.claude`; writes only to `tracking/`. Stores no prompt text,
57	  code or credentials.
58	- Known gaps: subscription-level `/usage` is not machine-readable; other project
59	  directories are out of scope; session end times are inferred, not reported.
60	
61	Full field definitions, limitations and verification evidence:
62	[docs/token-tracking.md](docs/token-tracking.md). Uncollectable sessions go in
63	[tracking/manual-sessions.md](tracking/manual-sessions.md) — never hand-edit the
64	generated ledger, and never invent historical usage.
65	
66	## Known documentation defect (unresolved, for Phase C)
67	`docs/asset-manifest.json` and `docs/reference-catalogue.md` list
68	`references/photography/landing-page-photo.jpg` and `workout-02.jpg`, but those
69	files are `.png` on disk. The documentation is wrong, not the assets. Fix the
70	docs in Phase C; never rename or overwrite a reference asset.
71	
72	## Product facts
73	SWO is a wearable-free, mobile-first training decision-support app. It uses sleep quality, fatigue/stiffness, and workout performance history with training frameworks to provide exercise-level Green / Amber / Red guidance. Public name: Smart Workout Optimizer (SWO). “Training Decision Validator” is an internal project/assignment label, not the public brand.
74	
75	## Design direction
76	- Product-first hero on a light/neutral background.
77	- Ink/navy text, restrained teal accent, cool neutral surfaces.
78	- Use real supplied SWO screenshots as product previews.
79	- Use personal gym photography selectively in supporting sections.
80	- Use Green / Amber / Red only as semantic decision states, not decoration.
81	- Keep layouts spacious and alternate text/image sections.
82	- Design mobile-first and maintain readable contrast and keyboard accessibility.
83	- Do not copy competitor branding, wording, or assets into the implementation.
84	
85	## Content and claims
86	- Primary audience: individual gym-goers and serious lifters.
87	- Explain recommendation rationale alongside status.
88	- Distinguish sports-science concepts from SWO's own implementation.
89	- Do not invent testimonials, adoption metrics, scientific validation, medical claims, or support channels.
90	- Do not imply the marketing mockups are a live connected product.
91	
92	## Acceptance tests
93	- Design tokens trace to explicit rules in `docs/style-guide.md` and a reference in `docs/reference-catalogue.md`.
94	- Structured content validates against a declared schema/rule set and renders correctly.
95	- The design-system subagent catches three planted violations and cites exact rules.
96	- A fresh Claude Code session understands the project from this file without foundational re-explanation.
97	- A custom skill is applied to a real task with before/after evidence.
98	- Keep a clear record of decisions, validation results, and evidence.
99	- Token/session totals come from `npm run track:usage`; re-run it before quoting a figure rather than reusing a number from a document.
100	
101	## Working principles
102	- Prefer small, reusable components over duplicated page-specific styles.
103	- Avoid arbitrary one-off values where a documented token exists.
104	- Do not claim tests passed unless they were actually run and results observed.
105	- Ask before expanding scope or introducing dependencies that materially change the project.

1	# Design-system audit rules
2	
3	The rule catalogue used by the `design-system-auditor` subagent
4	([.claude/agents/design-system-auditor.md](../.claude/agents/design-system-auditor.md)).
5	Every audit finding must cite one of these IDs plus the source document that
6	establishes the rule. If a problem does not fit a rule here, report it as an
7	**uncertain observation**, not a confirmed violation.
8	
9	Sources: [style-guide.md](style-guide.md) (tokens and component rules),
10	[component-reference.md](component-reference.md) (component APIs),
11	[content-model.md](content-model.md) (content rules), and the canonical token
12	file [src/styles/tokens.css](../src/styles/tokens.css).
13	
14	**Severity.** *High*: breaks accessibility, trust or the single token source.
15	*Medium*: breaks a documented convention. *Low*: minor drift.
16	
17	## Colour
18	
19	| ID | Rule | Source | Severity |
20	|---|---|---|---|
21	| DS-COLOR-01 | No hard-coded colour (hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, named colour, Tailwind arbitrary `[#…]`) in components. Use a semantic token. | style-guide.md, "Token reference → Colour"; tokens.css | High |
22	| DS-COLOR-02 | Components use semantic tokens only: no `--palette-*` reference and no default-Tailwind colour utility (`bg-red-500`, `text-gray-600`). | style-guide.md, "Token reference" intro | High |
23	| DS-COLOR-03 | `--color-brand-accent` is decorative. It must not colour text (3.55:1). | style-guide.md, `--color-brand-accent` | Medium |
24	| DS-COLOR-04 | `--color-border-default` is decorative. A form-control or button boundary must use `--color-border-strong`. | style-guide.md, `--color-border-default` | Medium |
25	| DS-STATE-01 | Green, Amber and Red are decision states, not decoration. They must not be used for branding, emphasis or ornament. | style-guide.md, "Design principles" and "Colour (semantic)" | High |
26	| DS-STATE-02 | Use `status-*` tokens for workout decisions and `feedback-*` tokens for UI messages. Do not use a green/amber/red token to mean something other than its state. | style-guide.md, "Why the feedback tokens alias the status tokens" | Medium |
27	
28	## Spacing, geometry and typography
29	
30	| ID | Rule | Source | Severity |
31	|---|---|---|---|
32	| DS-SPACE-01 | Spacing uses the documented steps (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16). No arbitrary `px`/`rem` values and no other numeric steps (`p-5`, `gap-10`). | style-guide.md, "Spacing, geometry and layout" | Medium |
33	| DS-TYPE-01 | Type uses the documented scale (`text-hero`, `text-h2`, `text-h3`, `text-body`, `text-small`) and `font-sans`. No arbitrary font size, `font-family`, or inline `fontSize`. | style-guide.md, "Typography" | Medium |
34	| DS-RADIUS-01 | Radius uses `rounded-card`, `rounded-button`, `rounded-control` or `rounded-pill`. No arbitrary radius. | style-guide.md, "Spacing, geometry and layout" | Low |
35	| DS-SHADOW-01 | Shadow uses `shadow-card` or `shadow-raised`. No arbitrary box-shadow. | style-guide.md, "Spacing, geometry and layout" | Low |
36	
37	## Components
38	
39	| ID | Rule | Source | Severity |
40	|---|---|---|---|
41	| DS-COMP-01 | Do not hand-build a pattern an existing component provides (button, card, badge, section container/heading, form field). Reuse it. | component-reference.md | Medium |
42	| DS-COMP-02 | Use only the documented variants and props of a component. No ad-hoc class overrides that recreate a different variant. | component-reference.md | Medium |
43	
44	## Accessibility
45	
46	| ID | Rule | Source | Severity |
47	|---|---|---|---|
48	| A11Y-01 | Status is never conveyed by colour alone. A Green/Amber/Red indicator needs a text label **and** an icon shape. Use `StatusBadge`. | style-guide.md, "Component rules → RAG status badge"; "Accessibility and trust" | High |
49	| A11Y-02 | Every form control has a visible label programmatically associated with it (`FormField`). Errors are text plus an icon, associated with the control. | style-guide.md, "Component rules → Forms" | High |
50	| A11Y-03 | Interactive elements are real `button`/`a` elements, keyboard operable, with a visible focus indicator. No `onClick` on a `div`/`span`; no `outline: none` without a replacement. | style-guide.md, "Accessibility and trust" | High |
51	| A11Y-04 | Every `img` has meaningful `alt` text, plus `width` and `height`. Decorative images use `alt=""`. | style-guide.md, "Component rules → Product preview" | High |
52	| A11Y-05 | Headings follow a logical order. A `section` used as a landmark has an accessible name (`aria-labelledby`/`aria-label`). | component-reference.md, `SectionContainer` | Medium |
53	| A11Y-06 | Interactive targets are at least `--min-target-size` (2.75rem) tall. | style-guide.md, `--min-target-size` | Medium |
54	| A11Y-07 | No placeholder link (`href="#"`, empty, `javascript:`) and no link without a real destination. | style-guide.md, "Component rules → FAQ/help links" | Medium |
55	
56	## Responsive layout
57	
58	| ID | Rule | Source | Severity |
59	|---|---|---|---|
60	| RESP-01 | Layout is mobile-first and never forces horizontal scrolling: no fixed pixel widths on containers, no `w-screen`/`min-w-[…]` wider than a phone, stacked on narrow screens with breakpoint prefixes widening it. | style-guide.md, "Responsive rules" | Medium |
61	| RESP-02 | Media keeps its aspect ratio and declares `width`/`height`. Do not crop essential UI text. | style-guide.md, "Responsive rules" | Low |
62	
63	## Content
64	
65	| ID | Rule | Source | Severity |
66	|---|---|---|---|
67	| CONTENT-01 | Marketing content is rendered only after `validateSiteContent()`. Components take the validated `SiteContent` type; they must not import `site-content.json` or a literal and render it directly. | content-model.md, "The boundary" | High |
68	| CONTENT-02 | No unsupported claims or fabricated trust signals: no testimonials, user counts, endorsements, guaranteed outcomes, injury prediction/prevention, clinical or scientific validation, or medical claims. | CLAUDE.md "Content and claims"; content-model.md | High |
69	| CONTENT-03 | Marketing copy is not hard-coded in JSX. Headings, paragraphs, CTAs, FAQ and feature text come from structured content. | content-model.md, "Why structured content" | Medium |
70	| CONTENT-04 | Do not imply the mockups are a live connected product. | CLAUDE.md "Content and claims" | Medium |
71	
72	## What this catalogue cannot decide
73	
74	Whether a sentence is *true*, whether a design *looks* right, or whether
75	real assistive technology works. The auditor reads code. It does not run it, and
76	it must say so.

2	
3	**Status.** Design tokens are **implemented** in [`src/styles/tokens.css`](../src/styles/tokens.css), the single canonical source. This guide documents them and records which v0.1 proposals were kept, which were changed and why, and what is still unverified.
4	
5	The two files are kept in step by tests (`npm test`): every token in `tokens.css` must appear in the reference table below with its exact declared value, and a documented token that no longer exists fails the build. Contrast is measured, not asserted (`npm run check:tokens`).
6	
7	Component APIs are in [component-reference.md](component-reference.md). Content rules are in [content-model.md](content-model.md). Reference → rule → token → component traces are in [traceability-matrix.md](traceability-matrix.md).
8	
9	## Decision status legend
10	
11	| Label | Meaning |
12	|---|---|
13	| **kept** | v0.1 proposal implemented unchanged and verified where it can be |
14	| **adjusted** | v0.1 proposal changed after measurement; the evidence is given |
15	| **added** | not in v0.1; needed by the implementation |
16	| **proposed** | implemented as a working default but **not validated** against a real layout or user need |
17	
18	Nothing marked **proposed** should be treated as a settled design decision.
19	
20	## Design principles
21	
22	1. **Product first:** show what SWO does before relying on lifestyle imagery.
23	2. **Explain the decision:** status, rationale and suggested action are visually distinct.
24	3. **Calm precision:** neutral canvas, confident typography, restrained accents.
25	4. **Evidence over hype:** explain frameworks and limits; avoid unsupported promises.
26	5. **Responsive by default:** content order and screenshots remain understandable on narrow screens.
27	6. **Accessible meaning:** status is conveyed by text and an icon shape as well as colour.
28	
29	## What the references showed

34	|---|---|---|

36	| The app's primary button uses **dark text on teal**, not white | APP-02 (`Finish`) | White-on-`#0F9986` is only 3.55:1, so the website CTA uses a darker teal that supports white text |
37	| Status pills always combine an **icon and a text label** (`⚠ CAUTION ZONE`, `✓ GREEN`, `✕ RED`) | APP-03, APP-06 | Implemented as a rule: `StatusBadge` always renders text and a distinct icon shape |
38	| Cards use large, soft radii; controls are rounded | APP-02, APP-06 | `--radius-card` (1rem) and `--radius-control` kept from v0.1 |
39	| Recommendation panels read: status, then reason, then a suggested next target | APP-02, APP-03 | Component rule "status → rationale → action" kept |

225	## Component rules
226	
227	- **Primary CTA:** `--color-brand-primary` fill with `--color-brand-on-primary` text, a clear action label, visible focus, a hit area of at least `--min-target-size`. One primary CTA per hero.
228	- **Secondary CTA:** outlined with `--color-border-strong`, visually quieter than the primary. Never two primary buttons competing.
229	- **Feature section:** pair a concise heading and explanatory copy with one meaningful screenshot; alternate layout direction.
230	- **Product preview:** preserve screenshot aspect ratio, avoid cropping essential UI text, give descriptive alt text, declare `width` and `height`, and label illustrative content.
231	- **RAG status badge:** text label **and** a distinct icon shape; colour alone is never sufficient.
232	- **Recommendation panel:** present status, rationale, then suggested action, in that order.
233	- **Metrics:** label, value, and unit or context.
234	- **Forms:** every control has a visible label; hints and errors are programmatically associated; an error is shown with an icon and text, never colour alone.
235	- **FAQ/help links:** clear labels, and only real destinations.
236	
237	## Responsive rules
238	
239	- Mobile first. On narrow screens, stack text and media vertically, text first.
240	- Never require horizontal scrolling. Measured on the showcase and content demo at 1280, 768 and 390px by `npm run capture`: no overflow at any of them.
241	- Body copy stays comfortably readable; buttons and controls stay at least `--min-target-size` tall.
242	- Screenshots stay legible; crop only when the crop hides nothing essential.
243	- Honour `prefers-reduced-motion` (implemented globally).
244	
245	## Accessibility and trust
246	
247	- Maintain WCAG AA contrast for text, verified against actual token pairs.
248	- Visible keyboard focus on every interactive element (global rule), semantic headings and landmarks.
249	- Convey Green/Amber/Red with label and icon shape, never colour alone.
250	- Do not claim medical diagnosis, injury prediction, clinical validation, guaranteed results or customer outcomes without substantiation. `src/content/schema.ts` rejects the most direct forms of these claims; see [content-model.md](content-model.md) for what that guard cannot catch.
251	- Distinguish published sports-science frameworks from SWO's own algorithm and product behaviour. The content schema makes both fields required for every framework.
252	
253	## Still unverified
254	
255	- **Typeface.** Inter is named but not loaded.
256	- **Breakpoints, shadows, focus-ring size.** Working defaults, not checked against a built page layout.
257	- **Contrast of imagery.** Text placed over photographs has not been designed yet, so no photo-overlay contrast is claimed.
258	- **Dark mode.** Not designed or implemented.
259	- **Real-device and screen-reader testing.** Only automated checks and a headless-browser capture have been run. No assistive technology has been used.

1	# Structured content model
2	
3	The marketing page renders from structured content, not from copy typed into JSX.
4	This document describes the model, the validation rules and the boundary.
5	
6	| Piece | Location |
7	|---|---|
8	| Schema and rules (Zod) | [`src/content/schema.ts`](../src/content/schema.ts) |
9	| Validation boundary | [`src/content/validate.ts`](../src/content/validate.ts) |
10	| Sample dataset | [`src/content/site-content.json`](../src/content/site-content.json) |
11	| Command-line check | `npm run validate:content` ([`scripts/validate-content.ts`](../scripts/validate-content.ts)) |
12	| Rendering demonstration | [`src/dev/ContentDemo.tsx`](../src/dev/ContentDemo.tsx), page `dev/content-demo.html` |
13	| Tests | `tests/content-schema.test.ts`, `tests/content-render.test.tsx` |
14	
15	## Why structured content
16	
17	Headings, paragraphs, calls to action, FAQ and feature copy live in data. That
18	keeps wording reviewable in one place, lets validation reject unsupported claims
19	before they reach a page, and keeps presentation components free of copy.
20	
21	## The boundary
22	
23	```
24	raw JSON  ->  validateSiteContent(input: unknown)  ->  { ok: true, data: SiteContent }
25	                                                     | { ok: false, issues: ContentIssue[] }
26	```
27	
28	- Raw content enters as `unknown`. Only the `ok: true` branch yields a
29	  `SiteContent`, so a component typed to take `SiteContent` cannot receive
30	  unvalidated data through normal code.
31	- Invalid content is **never partially rendered, patched or silently repaired**.
32	  There is no `data` on the failure branch.
33	- Each issue carries a dotted `path` (`faq[2].answer`) and a message that says
34	  what to change.
35	- `npm run build` runs `validate:content` first, so a build with invalid content
36	  fails.
37	
38	`validate:content` additionally checks what a schema cannot: every referenced
39	image exists under `public/` and its declared `width`/`height` equal the real
40	file's.
41	
42	## Sections
43	
44	| Key | Contents |
45	|---|---|
46	| `meta` | Page title and description |
47	| `hero` | Headline, supporting copy, primary and optional secondary CTA, preview image |
48	| `problem` | The training-guesswork framing and up to five points |
49	| `howItWorks` | 3 to 5 steps, each tagged `input`, `analysis` or `guidance` |
50	| `statuses` | Exactly three: `green`, `amber`, `red`, each with label, meaning, example rationale and suggested action |
51	| `features` | 1 to 6 sections, each with a product image and `imageSide` |
52	| `methodology` | Frameworks (concept **and** SWO implementation), an evidence status, and a disclaimer |
53	| `faq` | 3 to 10 question/answer pairs |
54	| `footer` | Link groups and a legal note |
55	
56	## Rules enforced
57	
58	| Rule | Behaviour |
59	|---|---|
60	| Required fields | A missing field is reported as `is required` at its exact path |
61	| Types | A wrong type reports what was received: `must be text (received a number)` |
62	| **Unknown fields rejected** | Objects are strict. A misspelt `headlne` is an error, not silently dropped |
63	| Lengths | Every text field has a minimum and maximum, stated in the message |
64	| Links | Only `#section`, `/path` or `https://…`. Rejected: `#`, empty, `javascript:`, `mailto:`/`tel:`, plain `http://`, protocol-relative, whitespace, and placeholder hosts such as `example.com` or `localhost` |
65	| Anchors | An in-page link must target a real section id (`#hero`, `#problem`, `#how-it-works`, `#status`, `#product`, `#science`, `#faq`) |
66	| CTAs | The secondary CTA may not duplicate the primary's destination |
67	| Images | `src` must be an optimised path under `/images/`. Alt text is at least 20 characters and must not start with "image of" or "screenshot of". `width`/`height` are required whole numbers |
68	| Status triple | Green, Amber and Red each exactly once, each with rationale and action. This builds in "explain the status, don't just colour it" |
69	| Framework vs implementation | Every framework needs both `concept` (the published idea) and `swoImplementation` (what SWO does). They cannot be blurred |
70	| Evidence status | `evidenceStatus: "sourced"` requires at least one https source. `framework-description-only` makes no evidential claim and is rendered as such |
71	| Flow | `howItWorks` must include an input, an analysis and a guidance step |
72	| Uniqueness | Ids within a list are unique; FAQ questions are unique |
73	| **Claim guard** | Rejects affirmative unsupported claims (below) |
74	
75	### The claim guard, and its limits
76	
77	Text fields are scanned for phrases that assert what SWO cannot substantiate:
78	`guarantee(d)`, `clinically proven/validated`, `scientifically proven/validated`,
79	`proven`, predicting/preventing/reducing injury, `cures/treats/diagnoses`,
80	adoption figures (`10,000 lifters`), `trusted by`/`endorsed by`/`featured in`/
81	`testimonial`, and professional endorsements (`coach-recommended`).
82	
83	A match is **ignored when a negation appears within 40 characters before it**, so a
84	disclaimer such as "does not diagnose, treat or prevent injury" and "has not been
85	clinically validated" is allowed.
86	
87	This is a pattern-based safety net, not editorial review:
88	
89	- It **cannot tell whether a sentence is true.** A false claim in plain wording
90	  passes.
91	- It is English-only and misses paraphrase ("works every time" is not caught).
92	- The negation window can wrongly excuse a claim placed after an unrelated "not".
93	
94	**Copy must still be reviewed by a person.** In particular, every
95	`swoImplementation` statement in the sample dataset is **draft copy that the
96	project owner must confirm** describes how SWO really works; nothing in the
97	repository establishes the algorithm's details.
98	
99	## Sample dataset notes
100	
101	`site-content.json` is realistic, not final. It deliberately contains:
102	
103	- no testimonials, user counts, pricing, download links, support email or other
104	  contact channel (none is confirmed);
105	- no external citations (`evidenceStatus` is `framework-description-only` for all
106	  three frameworks) because none has been verified;
107	- in-page anchor CTAs only, since no destination outside the page is confirmed.
108	
109	## Adding content
110	
111	1. Edit `src/content/site-content.json`.
112	2. Run `npm run validate:content`. Fix every reported path.
113	3. If you add an image, generate it with the `optimize-web-images` skill and copy
114	   its `width`/`height` from `public/images/manifest.json`.
